s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core in a patient with immunocompromised state
salient_findings: Tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions on lower and upper limbs
Lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core
Histopathological examination showing angioinvasive microbial structures and hyphal mats
key_facts: Patient is a 74-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
Patient has a complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
Patient was receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement
Patient was hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis in May 2022
Patient developed grade 4 neutropenia for over 15 days
Patient had a febrile peak
Skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
Histopathological examination showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation
Histopathological examination showed minimal necrosis and thrombosed small vessels
Histopathological examination showed sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
Patient was started on oral itraconazole after biopsy

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, consistent with Mucormycosis

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, which can be seen in Aspergillosis

shortlist.label: Fusariosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neutropenia and developed skin lesions, which can be seen in Fusariosis

shortlist.label: Scedosporiosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions, which can be seen in Scedosporiosis

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation and minimal necrosis, which can be seen in Blastomycosis

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions, which can be seen in Histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions, which can be seen in Candidiasis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions, which can be seen in Cryptococcosis

raw.rationale: The presence of angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in the histopathological examination, along with the patient's immunocompromised state due to chronic lymphocytic leukemia and neutropenia, are consistent with Mucormycosis. The description of thin-walled, pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching and thick-walled ovoid sporangia also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: Aspergillosis typically shows more branching and septate hyphae, which is not consistent with the histopathological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Fusariosis
rejected.why: Fusariosis is less likely given the presence of sporangial-type cells and the specific histopathological features described, which are more characteristic of Mucormycosis.

rejected.label: Scedosporiosis
rejected.why: Scedosporiosis is less likely due to the lack of characteristic features such as slender, branched hyphae and the presence of sporangial-type cells, which are more consistent with Mucormycosis.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with thick-walled, broad-based budding yeast forms, which were not described in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis typically presents with small, intracellular yeast forms, which were not described in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Candidiasis
rejected.why: Candidiasis typically presents with pseudohyphae and blastoconidia, which were not described in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Cryptococcosis typically presents with encapsulated yeast forms, which were not described in the histopathological examination.
